title: Broccoli, cauliflower and carrots, cooked, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Broccoli, cauliflower and carrots are vegetables often combined as a ready‑to‑eat mix. Cooking them without added fat preserves their natural flavor and nutrients, making the dish low‑calorie and rich in vitamins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Broccoli and cauliflower belong to the cruciferous family and contain compounds that support the body’s detoxification processes.
Carrots are one of the richest sources of beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
The trio is a staple in diet plans because of its low calorie density and high fiber content.
Steaming without fat retains over 90 % of vitamin C in broccoli and cauliflower.
These vegetables pair well with a wide range of herbs, spices, and low‑fat sauces.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Broccoli and cauliflower provide vitamin B6, while carrots supply vitamin B2, both important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamin C and antioxidants in broccoli and cauliflower help strengthen the immune system.

items.title: Eye health
items.content: Beta‑carotene from carrots is converted to vitamin A, essential for good vision.

items.title: Reduced risk of chronic disease
items.content: Cruciferous vegetables contain sulforaphane, which is being studied for its anti‑cancer properties.

items.title: Digestive health
items.content: Fiber from all three vegetables promotes regular bowel movements and contributes to satiety.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Cruciferous vegetables can cause increased gas production in people with sensitive digestion.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may be allergic to broccoli or cauliflower.

items.title: Nutrient loss with overcooking
items.content: Excessive boiling can reduce vitamin C and some phytochemicals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Steam or boil the vegetables without added fat until tender. They work well in salads, soups, stews, or as a standalone side dish. A squeeze of lemon, fresh herbs, or a light yogurt‑based sauce can enhance flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh vegetables in the refrigerator’s crisper drawer, stored in a perforated bag. Store the cooked mix in an airtight container for up to 3‑4 days.
